native.text: Prerequisites: {facts.runtime_requirements}.
Commit the lockfiles: {facts.lockfiles}.
Locking excludes `{facts.generated_cache_directory}` from the native build context. Also commit the updated ignore file.
The native lock records exact revisions; its companion records artifact hashes, original metadata, and resolution configuration.
OCI manifest, configuration, and layer identities retain their native SHA-256 digests. The lock adds platform selections and input fingerprints.

locked.text:
Run `{commands.lock}` after changing dependency declarations. Relocking retains existing pins.

Run `{commands.update}` to update dependencies, then `{commands.prefetch}`.
Update one selected dependency with `{commands.named-update} {facts.named_update_example}`. Other selected pins are retained.

fresh.text:
Run `{commands.lock}` after changing dependency declarations. Relocking resolves dependencies again; it does not retain existing pins.

Run `{commands.prefetch}` before building.
Update one selected dependency with `{commands.named-update} {facts.named_update_example}`. Other selected pins are retained.

native.text: Keep using the native build and test commands in your working tree. After changing dependency declarations, refresh the lock through the native lock workflow shown above.
Relocking retains existing pins.

wrapper.text: The shell supplies a wrapper for the native build tool. Without an applicable lock, it warns and runs the ordinary native tool. A stale or invalid lock fails with a repair command.
The supplied wrapper is required for native builds.
The integration handles {facts.supported_native_commands}; other native commands run normally.

Alternatively, activate the native plugin in the build. Resolve `{facts.native_plugin_coordinate}` from the [native plugin repository]({facts.native_plugin_repository}). Keep bootstrap dependencies separate from application dependencies.
Native Maven bootstrap resolution is impure; use the wrapper for pure plugin resolution.

native.text: The development environment supplies the native tools and their purifier integration. Use that environment for builds, tests, and editor processes so they share the selected dependencies.
Without an applicable lock, the integration warns and runs the ordinary native tool.
The native tool reads the prepared project dependencies directly; wrapper activation is not required.

scoped.text:
Run `{commands.prefetch}` to prepare the locked dependencies. This does not guarantee that the entire build can run offline.

Outside this lock: {facts.offline_limits}.
Prefetch retains {facts.prefetch_components} through garbage-collector roots beside the selected lockfile.

native.text: Prepare dependencies using the Quickstart workflow before disconnecting. The lock covers the recorded dependency downloads; downloads performed outside that lock need separate inputs.

command.text: Configure the Language Server Protocol (LSP) client to launch `{commands.editor}` from the development shell. This puts its language tooling in the same environment as the native build.
Diagnostics and definition lookup work offline after prefetch.
The language server can retrieve source code for locked dependencies.
The launcher prepares Eclipse project metadata with immutable dependency and source JAR paths.

native.text: Integration mechanism: {facts.editor_protocol}.
{values.language_tooling_setup}

builder.text:
Apply `overlays.default` and call `{facts.nix_builder}`.

The result exposes: {facts.build_outputs}.
The project builds in the Nix sandbox.
The builder runs {facts.build_engine} inside a networkless software VM.

native.text: Native development does not require a project Nix build definition. To build the whole project in the Nix sandbox, apply `overlays.default` and call `{facts.nix_builder}`.
The builder exposes: {facts.build_outputs}.

preparation.text: Call `{facts.nix_builder}` through `overlays.default` to prepare sources with their native dependency environment. Deployment remains a native tool operation.

directional.text: Incoming: this integration does not consume project projections.
Outgoing: this integration does not export project projections.

platforms.text: The default CLI transport supports anonymous access. Builder fetcher overrides can integrate corporate transport.

versionCompatibility.title: Version compatibility
versionCompatibility.unknown: The Quickstart uses the purifier’s pinned Nix toolchain. Exact tool, project runtime/compiler and helper versions, and supported version ranges, have not yet been recorded for this purifier.
versionCompatibility.introduction: The Quickstart uses the purifier’s pinned Nix toolchain. Tested combinations below distinguish the native tool, its runtime, the project runtime/compiler and capture/build helpers.
versionCompatibility.noRanges: **Supported ranges:** No reviewed version range is recorded.
versionCompatibility.noTests: No version-specific test combinations are recorded yet.
versionCompatibility.pointScope: These checks cover only the listed versions, platforms and operations. They do not establish a minimum version or compatibility between tested points.
